title: Optimistic late-bind decode planner: kernel-aware model routing, probe acceptance metrics, and staged fallback
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build an optimistic, late-bind decode planning layer that can route requests to the fastest compatible model/kernel variant by using a lightweight preexecution probe and an acceptance metric. Provide a staged fallback to more conservative decoders when the acceptance signal indicates low confidence or kernel mismatch. Goal: reduce tail latency for common short generation workloads while preserving correctness and predictable degrade behavior.
scope: In scope: probe token execution, kernel affinity signal, lightweight acceptance scoring, routing decision API, soft-commit logic, telemetry for acceptance & rollback. Out of scope: full multi-turn session transfer, quantization changes at runtime, new model weight uploads.
design_decisions: Use a 1-2 token probe executed on candidate kernel variants to derive kernel latency + early logits agreement as acceptance signal.
Late-bind routing: select a candidate model+kernel at the last possible moment using recent scheduler metrics and probe results, rather than pinning at request start.

Soft-commit: allow the optimistic path to continue decoding for N tokens while monitoring a rolling acceptance score; on low score, trigger graceful handoff to conservative path with token reconciliation.
Kernel affinity is treated as a first-class signal: prefer kernels with <p50 latency for the request profile, but fall back based on acceptance score, not purely latency.
Acceptance metrics combine (a) probe relative latency, (b) top-k logit overlap with conservative model on probe tokens, and (c) decode divergence heuristics over initial tokens.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end routing decision completes within 2ms added overhead relative to baseline request path.
Optimistic path reduces 95th percentile latency by >=10% for short (<=64 tokens) generations on benchmark workloads.
Fallback handoff completes without losing coherent output: at most 2 token reconciliation edits on average when handoff occurs.
All acceptance & fallback events emitted to runtime telemetry with unique event ids for traceability.
Feature gated behind runtime flag and can be toggled per-customer and per-route.
implementation_plan: 1) Add probe API to scheduler that can dispatch a 1-token preexecution to a tiny candidate kernel instance and return latency+logits.
2) Implement acceptance scorer service that computes combined score and exposes threshold configuration via config store.
3) Extend route chooser to support late-bind selection and maintain per-request local state for optimistic soft-commit.
4) Implement graceful handoff protocol: token queue snapshot, conservative decode resume, and minimal edit reconciliation.
5) Integrate with kernel telemetry to fetch recent p50/p95 latencies for consideration in routing decision.
6) Add feature flag and per-customer controls in config; default off for public hosted API until rollout validation.
testing_plan: Unit tests for probe API, acceptance scorer logic, and handoff protocol edge cases.
Integration tests that synthesize mismatch scenarios: kernel slowdowns, model divergence, and transient errors to validate fallback correctness.
Load tests in staging with mixed request profiles to ensure probe overhead does not regress throughput under sustained load.
A/B experiment: 5% traffic optimistic route vs control for 48 hours measuring latency, token cost, and quality deltas on held-out prompts.
Chaos test: inject kernel stalls and verify acceptance score triggers rollback with no unbounded retries.
rollout_plan: Canary 5% internal traffic (dev and seeding customers) for 72 hours, monitor latency and reconciliation rate.
Expand to 20% with feature gate on low-risk routes (short completions) and observe metrics for 7 days.
Enable per-customer opt-in with dashboard controls in Console and warn customers about potential reconciliation edits in logs.
Full enable across short-generation routes if reconciliation rate <1% and no customer regressions observed.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probe overhead increases tail latency under high contention. Mitigation: fallback to disabled probe under high queue depth; monitor queue-length signals.
Risk: Acceptance score false negatives cause unnecessary handoffs and wasted work. Mitigation: tune scoring weights and add hysteresis to prevent flip-flopping.
Risk: Reconciliation can produce nonsensical final output if token alignment fails. Mitigation: limit handoff to first N tokens and fall back to conservative full-recompute beyond that.
Risk: Increased cost due to double decode work on handoffs. Mitigation: expose per-route cost cap and sampling-based audit to measure actual extra tokens.

comments: 2026-02-21 - Marcus Lee: Spiked a probe microbenchmark. 1-token probe adds ~0.8ms median on A100 but variance depends on kernel warm state. Sharing numbers in PR.
2026-02-25 - Sofia Patel (PM): Aligning acceptance target: prefer fewer false handoffs even if it reduces optimistic wins; customers value quality over small latency wins.
2026-03-02 - Anika Rao (SRE): Load test showed probe causes queue build-up at 95th under peak. Proposed fast-disable switch when queue depth > 50 per GPU.
2026-03-05 - Marcus Lee: Implemented probe API and acceptance scorer prototype; submitted PR 1173. Need review from kernel team on safe probe execution semantics.
2026-03-09 - Kernel Team (Jamal Ortiz): Reviewed PR. Concern: some kernels return non-deterministic logits for 1-token probe due to fused ops; recommended adding jitter-tolerant overlap metric.
2026-03-12 - Marcus Lee: Adjusted acceptance scorer to incorporate logits similarity with tolerance. Running canary internally tomorrow.
